sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface sortagging was successful, confirming the LPETG motif is accessible at the extracellular face; CD1d antigen-presentation function was NOT MEASURED for this tagged construct.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly places the insertion 'between the extracellular and the transmembrane domain' of mouse Cd1d1; for human CD1D the EC domain ends at residue 301 (S) and the TM begins at 302 (M), making 301|302 the unique EC/TM junction. The GS linker included in the construct provides physical spacing from the TM helix, and successful cell-surface sortagging confirms extracellular accessibility. Because the source is a mouse ortholog and no residue number is given, the position is classified as inferred rather than validated. Mouse Cd1d1 (close ortholog of human CD1D) was engineered with an LPETG SortA recognition motif plus a glycine/serine-based linker inserted between the extracellular domain and the transmembrane domain of the full-length, membrane-anchored protein, expressed in cells and subjected to cell-surface sortagging.

sources.claim: Sortase A-cleavable constructs were generated by inserting the SortA peptide recognition motif LPETG together with a glycine-/serine-based linker between the extracellular and the transmembrane domain of mouse Cd1d1 or H-2Kb .

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are two clips from the same paper (PMC9301999) describing the same construct; they are treated as a single site grounded in L2 (the more structurally precise clip). No ledger evidence supports an N-terminal tag (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 19) or any internal loop insertion for human CD1D. The >=3-residue-from-TM geometric constraint is formally at its limit here (insert_after_residue 301 is the last EC residue), but the published GS linker provides the required physical spacing and the sortagging result confirms surface accessibility, so the site is retained with medium confidence.
